The browser requests another user's avatar via the URL `/file/{user-resource-name}/avatar` — the frontend `UserAvatar` renders ``, and that `avatarUrl` is rewritten by the API's user converter to point at the fileserver endpoint (rather than embedding the raw base64), so the `` fetch lands on the Go fileserver route. From there it walks down through the store into the SQL driver, which reads the `avatar_url` column; the handler then base64-decodes that stored data URI and writes the image bytes back. Hops: `` — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:12 `convertUserToProto` sets `AvatarUrl = "/file/{name}/avatar"` — server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36 `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` route → `serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 `serveUserAvatar()` handler — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 `s.getUserByUsername()` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:185 (defined at :715) `s.Store.GetUser(FindUser{Username})` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:716 → store/user.go:148 `s.ListUsers()` — store/user.go:158 (defined at :136) `s.driver.ListUsers()` — store/user.go:137 `(*DB).ListUsers()` SQL query reading `avatar_url` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (also mysql/user.go:84, postgres/user.go:87) `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` decodes stored base64 → `c.Blob(...)` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196, 209 Note the access gate: on a non-anonymous instance `serveUserAvatar` first requires an authenticated viewer (fileserver.go:173–181) before serving another user's avatar.
